findings.reason: the strictness decision the plan waits on is partly already made in code, so the remaining work is an extension of a named owner, not a new subsystem, and M1's "blocked" status overstates what is missing.
findings.text: §3.1 / §4 M1 list "write-time lifecycle invariants" as unbuilt and blocked, but `validate_landing_patch` (`reckon/_store.py:3316`), `_require_terminal_evidence` (`reckon/_store.py:3333`, `reckon/_store.py:1417`) and `apply_ops` (`reckon/_store.py:3396`) already refuse a terminal or landing write that names no continuation or no `docs/evidence/archive/<slug>-landed.html` record, and are wired onto the live write path at `reckon/serve.py:3580`; the plan must state whether §3.1 extends these or replaces them

findings.reason: §3.3 collapses to "wire the existing command to a cron", deleting a proposed mechanism and its M3 milestone.
findings.text: §3.3 / §4 M3 report the "automated sweep" as still pending and propose a quarterly `plan-archived=1` pass, but `run_archive_pass` (`reckon/archive.py:146`) plus `reckon archive --apply` (`reckon/cli.py:8126`) already implement exactly that age-thresholded pass; the only missing piece is a scheduler, not the sweep

findings.reason: the close gate should extend one owner (a single sprint-readiness predicate) rather than add a scan the plan itself concedes will duplicate a rule.
findings.text: §3.5's sprint-close gate would add a third sprint-eligibility scan beside the two that already exist — `reckon/mcp.py:2291 _audit_sprint_findings` and the roadmap scan at `reckon/roadmap.py:2675`, which already share the `CLOSED_SPRINT_STATUSES` vocabulary at `reckon/roadmap.py:1939` — the plan names no owner and so invites a fork of the unresolved-followup / unset-impl logic

findings.reason: the WARN and ERROR halves belong on the existing audit module, so §3.1 should route detection through it rather than describe a second detector.
findings.text: §3.1's "status shipped/done + no section-landed card ⟹ WARN on write + audit ERROR after N days" duplicates the landed-summary / render-contract audit already owned by `reckon/doccheck.py::audit_lifecycle` (`reckon/doccheck.py:488) and `_LANDED_SECTION_CLASS` (`reckon/doccheck.py:116`); the plan re-authors the check instead of naming this owner

findings.reason: §3.2's deliverable is a scheduler and a report surface, not a new sweep, and saying so removes a mechanism from the plan.
findings.text: §3.2 proposes a "staleness sweep" that flags active plans older than 30 days with impl < 1.0, but `reckon audit` (`reckon/cli.py:7981`) and `audit_lifecycle` already compute that exact STALE list (threshold at `reckon/doccheck.py:150`); the plan adds a re-reader where the honest change is to schedule the existing command

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — no module is named to own lifecycle invariants; the six milestones spread the behaviour across the server write path, the MCP audit, the plan-creation skill and the sprint-close path, with no single interface hiding it.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §3.5's sprint-close gate and §3.1's terminal-state checks re-implement eligibility scans that already have owners (`reckon/_store.py`, `reckon/roadmap.py`, `reckon/mcp.py`), so the plan should extend those owners rather than add a parallel scan.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan proposes §3.1 write-time invariants, §3.2 audit cadence and §3.3 archive waves as mechanisms to build, but each already ships: `reckon/_store.py` write validation, `reckon/doccheck.py::audit_lifecycle`, and `reckon/archive.py::run_archive_pass` respectively; the plan cites none of them as the thing to extend.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §3.2's "staleness sweep" re-derives the exact STALE / MISSING_IMPL / STALE_RCA list `reckon/doccheck.py::audit_lifecycle` already produces, so the proposed sweep is a thin re-read over an existing reader rather than an extension of it.
